content: Book-keeper to the Lord Chamberlain's Men; keeps the prompt book, parts, and plots.
The plot stays on the door. He will not let the morning mend the book.
He will head a margin with a K and he will not write a figure he has not counted.
He will not invent a total before a yard has heard the play, and he reads eleven once it is written.
He will add eleven and thirteen into twenty-four, and he will not add a song the yard did not hear.
He will not tick a tune sung at a bench, and he will say thirty-five and one song after the yard without copying the lines that night.
From the next table, Kemp's interest is nineteen lines, and a noise like a goose.
When he stops at fifteen, ask what he was counting. This Monday it was the yard breaking the hush, not a new total of Kemp's lines.
No new tick on the tally. Nineteen lines, and a noise like a goose, still.
He will take a king in a shirt, refuse a cousin's manners, and keep the six days.
He asks the book to hear a change, and he does not decide it.
